## Goal

By the end of this exercise you should have:

- **Quarto** installed, with the agent's help,
- a small **Quarto website** for the example project, with a sidebar, a results page with a figure, a slide deck and an about page,
- that site **published on GitHub Pages** from the `docs/` folder of a public repository, and **checked live**,
- a clear answer to **what became public**, and why the example project itself stayed private,
- a **page for your own project or one of your courses**, with your figures from *Reproducible figures* as the first content, published, and
- the link **sent to a colleague**, who has opened it.

Your session will look different from anyone else's. Compare **results**, not sessions.

## Before you start

- You finished the *GitHub* exercise: `gh auth status` says you are logged in, and `~/agentic-course/plant-growth/` exists with its figure `results/growth_plot.png` (if not, download [plant-growth.zip](../github/data/plant-growth.zip) and unzip it into your course folder).
- Your own project has at least one figure made by a script (*Reproducible figures*) and is a private repository on GitHub (*GitHub*).
- Know your GitHub **username**: it becomes part of the address, `https://<username>.github.io/...`.

## Worked example

We build a page for the synthetic plant-growth project. The project repository stays **private**: in the GitHub exercise you saw that its history still contains `notes/contacts.txt`. So the page gets its **own, separate repository**, which will be public and hold only what we choose.

### Step 1: Install Quarto

Start the agent in your **course folder** and type:

```text
Is Quarto installed? If not, install it with the official method for
my operating system. Explain each command before you run it. Then run
quarto --version.
```

**What to look for.** On a Mac the agent often proposes `brew install --cask quarto` or downloading the installer from [quarto.org](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/); on Windows `winget` or the installer. An installer may open a system window asking for your computer password: type it there, never into the agent. If your computer is managed by your university and the install is blocked, ask IT, or install from [quarto.org](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/) yourself.

#### Check the result

`quarto --version` prints a version number (for example 1.8 or higher). If it says "command not found", close the terminal, open a new one and try again.

### Step 2: Make the page folder and start the agent there

Exit the agent (`/exit`). Make a new, empty folder next to `plant-growth` and start the agent in it:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Claude Code
```bash
mkdir ~/agentic-course/plant-growth-page
cd ~/agentic-course/plant-growth-page
claude
```
Use a mode that asks before commands (Shift+Tab; Manual is fine).

## Codex
```bash
mkdir ~/agentic-course/plant-growth-page
cd ~/agentic-course/plant-growth-page
codex
```
The folder is not a git repository yet, so Codex may start read-only. Type `/permissions` and choose the level that lets it edit files in the workspace (not full access).
:::

### Step 3: Let the agent scaffold the site

```text
Make a Quarto website in this folder for the example project in
../plant-growth. Read ../plant-growth/README.md and look at its figure,
but do not change anything in ../plant-growth.

Pages, in this order in a sidebar:
- Home (index.qmd): what the trial is, in 3 or 4 sentences. Say clearly
  that the data is synthetic.
- Results (results.qmd): the figure, copied from
  ../plant-growth/results/growth_plot.png into figures/, with a caption
  that names the script that made it. One short paragraph on what the
  figure shows, using only what the figure shows.
- About (about.qmd): "Made by <MY NAME>" as a placeholder, licence
  CC BY 4.0 for text and figures, and one sentence on how AI was used.

Settings: output-dir docs; an empty .nojekyll file, listed under project
resources so Quarto copies it into docs/; theme cosmo.
Also a README.md: what this repository is, how to render it, and which
commit of ../plant-growth the figure was copied from.
Copy nothing else from ../plant-growth. Then run quarto render and list
the files in docs/.
```

**What to look for.**

- The agent will ask to **read files outside its folder** (`../plant-growth`). That is expected here; approve reading, but it should not ask to write there. If it does, say no.
- It may run `quarto create project website` first and then change the files, or write them directly. Either is fine.
- To find the commit, it runs something like `git -C ../plant-growth log -1`. That only looks.

When it is done, open `_quarto.yml` and `results.qmd` in a text editor (or ask "show me _quarto.yml and results.qmd"). You should recognise the parts from the lecture: `output-dir: docs`, the sidebar list, the figure line `![...](figures/growth_plot.png)`.

### Step 4: Look at the site before anything is public

Open the folder in your file browser, go into `docs`, and double-click `index.html`. It opens in your web browser.

#### Check the result

1. The sidebar shows **Home, Results, About**, in that order, and each link works.
2. The Results page shows the figure, with a caption that names `scripts/plot_growth.py`.
3. The text on the Results page matches the figure. In week 6, the mean heights are about **19.4 cm (high_N), 17.8 cm (low_N) and 14.2 cm (control)**; all three start near **4 cm**. "High nitrogen grew fastest, control slowest" is right. Any claim about significance, p-values or "proves" is not supported by a figure and should go.
4. Home says the data is **synthetic**.
5. About has the placeholder for your name, **CC BY 4.0**, and one sentence on AI use.
6. In the `docs` folder there is a file `.nojekyll` (it may be hidden: on a Mac press Cmd+Shift+. in Finder; on Windows, View → Show → Hidden items).

Correct anything you do not like by saying what is wrong, for example:

```text
On the Results page, remove the sentence "the effect is significant":
a figure of means cannot show that. Replace the <MY NAME> placeholder
with "<your name>, <your department>". Render again.
```

### Step 5: Add a short slide deck

```text
Add slides.qmd with format revealjs: a title slide and three slides,
"The question", "The result" (the same figure) and "What next"
(one bullet: repeat with three bean lines). Put it in the sidebar
between Results and About as "Slides". Render again.
```

Open `docs/slides.html` in your browser. Press the right arrow to move through the slides, **F** for full screen and **Esc** to leave it.

### Step 6: Check what will become public

This repository will be public. Ask, before it exists on GitHub:

```text
I am going to publish this folder as a PUBLIC GitHub repository.
List every file that will be in it, and every file in docs/.
Flag anything that is personal, confidential, or that was not meant to
be published. Do not change anything.
```

#### Check the result

The list should hold only the page sources (`_quarto.yml`, the `.qmd` files, `README.md`, `.nojekyll`), `figures/growth_plot.png`, and the rendered `docs/` folder. There must be **no** `contacts.txt`, no `notes/`, no `data/`. If something else is there, ask the agent to remove it before the first commit.

### Step 7: Create the public repository and push

```text
Make this folder a git repository with the branch name main. Commit
everything, including docs/, with the message "First version of the
page". Then create a PUBLIC GitHub repository called plant-growth-page
from this folder and push. Show me each command before you run it.
```

Before you approve `gh repo create`, check: the name is `plant-growth-page` and it says `--public`. This time public is right: you checked the contents in step 6, and there is no history yet beyond this one commit.

Open `https://github.com/<your-username>/plant-growth-page`. The label next to the name says **Public**, and you see the files from step 6.

### Step 8: Switch on GitHub Pages

Choose **one** of the two ways.

**On the website.** In the repository: **Settings** → **Pages** (left menu). Under **Build and deployment**, set **Source** to **Deploy from a branch**, choose branch **main** and folder **/docs**, and click **Save**.

**With the agent.**

```text
Switch on GitHub Pages for this repository, serving the /docs folder of
the main branch. Use gh api. Then tell me the address of the site.
```

The agent proposes something like:

```bash
echo '{"source":{"branch":"main","path":"/docs"}}' | gh api -X POST repos/<your-username>/plant-growth-page/pages --input -
```

Check that the branch is `main` and the path is `/docs` before you approve.

### Step 9: Check the live site

Wait a minute or two. Refresh **Settings → Pages** until it says your site is live, or open the address directly:

`https://<your-username>.github.io/plant-growth-page/`

If you get a 404 error, wait another minute. If it persists, look at the **Actions** tab of the repository: a failed "pages build and deployment" run shows why.

#### Check the result

Do every check yourself; the agent cannot see your browser.

1. The address opens and shows your Home page.
2. Every sidebar link works: Home, Results, Slides, About.
3. The figure shows on the Results page.
4. The slides open and advance with the arrow keys.
5. Open the address in a **private browser window** (not logged in to GitHub). It looks the same.
6. Open it on your **phone**. The sidebar becomes a menu; the figure fits the screen.
7. Read every page once more as a stranger. Is there anything you would not want a student, a reviewer or a journalist to read?

### Step 10: Change something and publish again

```text
On the Home page, add one sentence at the end: "Last updated <today's
date>." Render the site, show me which files changed, then commit with
a clear message and push.
```

Wait a minute or two, then reload the live Home page (Shift+reload, or Cmd+Shift+R / Ctrl+F5, to skip the cache). The new sentence is there. This is the loop you will repeat in every later unit: **edit, render, look, commit, push, check live**.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Expected outcome for the worked example"}
- Folder `~/agentic-course/plant-growth-page/` with `_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd`, `results.qmd`, `slides.qmd`, `about.qmd`, `README.md`, `.nojekyll`, `figures/growth_plot.png` and `docs/` (with `index.html`, `results.html`, `slides.html`, `about.html`, `.nojekyll`, `search.json` and `site_libs/`).
- `_quarto.yml` contains `output-dir: docs`, a `resources` entry for `.nojekyll`, and a sidebar listing the four pages in the order Home, Results, Slides, About.
- A public repository `plant-growth-page` with 2 commits, and Pages serving `main` `/docs`.
- The live site at `https://<your-username>.github.io/plant-growth-page/`.
- The project repository `plant-growth` is still **private**, untouched.
:::

## On your own project

Now the same for your own project, or for one of your courses if your project is a course. The **first content is your figure from *Reproducible figures***.

### Step 11: Decide where the page lives

| If… | then… |
|---|---|
| everything in your project folder **and its whole history** may be public (for example open data, your own teaching material) | the page can live **in the project repository**, as this course's site does. You will have to make the project repository public. |
| anything in the project is internal, personal or confidential, or you have **not checked the history** | make a **separate page repository**, as in the worked example. This is the default. |

If you choose the same repository: ask the agent to list every file ever committed (as in step 9 of the *GitHub* exercise) and read the list before you go on. Also tell the agent to add a `render:` list to `_quarto.yml`, like this course's, so that notes, `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` and data are **not** rendered as pages: by default Quarto turns every `.qmd` and `.md` file in the folder into a page (except `README.md`).

### Step 12: Build the page

Make the folder (for example `~/agentic-course/soil-funding-map-page/`), start the agent there, and adapt this prompt:

```text
Make a Quarto website in this folder for my project in ../<my-project>.
Read ../<my-project>/README.md for the goal and the data class. Copy
only the files I name below, and nothing else.

Pages, in this order in a sidebar:
- Home: the goal of the project in plain words, for <who the page is for>.
- Results: the figure(s) <file names in ../<my-project>/results/>,
  copied into figures/, each with a caption that names the script and
  the data it came from.
- About: my name and <department>, a contact route (my university
  profile page: <link>), the licence (CC BY 4.0 for text and figures),
  where the data comes from, and one sentence on how AI was used.

Settings: output-dir docs; an empty .nojekyll listed under project
resources; theme cosmo. A README.md saying which commit of
../<my-project> each figure came from.
Render the site and list the files in docs/.
```

For a **course page**, use pages such as Home (what the course is, for whom), Schedule, Material (links to slides and exercises), and About. A slide deck (`format: revealjs`) for one lecture is a good second step.

Open `docs/index.html` and check it as in step 4. Then do the **public check** from step 6, against the **Never put in this folder** list in your project's README. A figure can also leak data: a plot with individual points labelled by student name, a map with a patient's home town. Look at each figure with that in mind.

### Step 13: Publish and check

Create the public page repository and push (step 7), switch on Pages (step 8), and go through the live checklist (step 9): every link, every figure, a private window, your phone, and a last read as a stranger.

### Step 14: Send the link to a colleague

Send the address to one colleague, for example:

> I am trying out a project page made with Quarto and GitHub Pages: https://&lt;username&gt;.github.io/&lt;repo&gt;/. Does it open for you, and is it clear what the project is about from the first page?

Their answer is the real test. Note any confusion as an issue on the page repository (*GitHub*), so it is on your to-do list.

Finally, add a line to the **Log of AI use** in your project README, for example: "2026-11-30, Codex (Plus): built and published the project page from my figures; I checked every page and figure." Add the page address to the project README too.

## What you should have now

- Quarto installed (`quarto --version` works).
- `plant-growth-page`: a public repository with a Quarto site, and a live page at `https://<your-username>.github.io/plant-growth-page/`, while `plant-growth` stays private.
- A **page for your own project or course**, live, with your figure from *Reproducible figures* as the first content, a caption that names its script, an About page with licence and AI-use statement, and nothing on it that should not be public.
- The link **sent to a colleague**, and their answer.
- The update loop in your hands: **edit, render, look, commit, push, check live**. In *Interactive demos* you add an interactive page to this site.
